fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled per-glyph variation offsets are read from the font's offsetZ array. In the PoC, offsets[0]==offsets[glyphCount]==0 makes the shallow sanitizer's data-range check zero-length (and vacuous), while glyph 0 yields start_offset=0, end_offset=4.

Flawed GlyphVarData fetch: the pointer is computed as this + dataZ + start_offset with no validation that dataZ + end_offset lies within the font blob. The only checks are start_offset <= get_offset(glyphCount) and start_offset + GlyphVarData::min_size <= end_offset, and because offsets[glyphCount]==offsets[0] the sanitized data range has length 0, so a huge dataZ (0xFFFF) passes sanitize and the returned reference points ~65KB past the end of the font buffer.
The out-of-bounds GlyphVarData reference is fetched for the glyph being shaped/drawn (gid 0) while applying variation deltas.
Sink: has_data() dereferences the first field (tupleVarCount) of the out-of-bounds GlyphVarData pointer, performing the invalid memory access (heap-buffer-overflow read).

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: oss-fuzz 20906: invalid memory access in the gvar table caused by the flawed GlyphVarData fetch logic; get_glyph_var_data returns this+dataZ+start_offset without bounding dataZ+end_offset against the font blob, and a zero-length sanitized data range (offsets[glyphCount]==offsets[0]) lets an oversized dataZ pass sanitize. The crafted gvar table sets dataZ=0xFFFF with per-glyph offsets [0,4] so glyph 0's GlyphVarData reference lands far past the buffer and has_data() reads it out of bounds.
